proposal: The Mandate recommends that the next administration work with Congress to eliminate DOE's applied energy and demonstration programs, naming EERE, the fossil energy and carbon management office, the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations, the Grid Deployment Office, the State and Community Energy Programs office and ARPA-E. Where an office survives, it should concentrate on fundamental science and energy security, and Congress should rescind excess unspent funds.
remaining: Congress would need to repeal or defund the statutory offices and programs (OCED and GDO were created under the IIJA; ARPA-E under the 2007 COMPETES Act); the FY2026 act zeroed OCED but continued to fund ARPA-E and EERE.
Rescind remaining unspent applied-energy appropriations; the FY2026 act reprogrammed about 5.16 billion dollars of unobligated IIJA funds rather than rescinding them (Holland & Knight).
Narrow the retained energy technology, demonstration and appliance divisions to the basic-science and security focus the Mandate describes as its fallback.
Resolve litigation over the award terminations.

status_summary: As of 2026-10-08 DOE has reorganized most of the named offices out of stand-alone existence, but Congress has not eliminated them and kept funding several in FY2026. DOE's organization chart dated 2025-11-20 does not show EERE, the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations, the Grid Deployment Office, the fossil energy office, the State and Community Energy Programs office, the Federal Energy Management Program or the Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains office as stand-alone offices; it shows a new Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, a Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office and ARPA-E as a stand-alone office. Holland & Knight reports that the Loan Programs Office became the Office of Energy Dominance Financing and that most EERE programs, including state and community programs and the Federal Energy Management Program, moved into the new innovation office. The FY2026 Energy and Water act is Division B of Public Law 119-74 (H.R. 6938, approved 2026-01-23); per Holland & Knight (summary written before signing) it gave the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations no appropriation, funded EERE at 3.1 billion dollars (including reprogrammed funds), ARPA-E at 350 million dollars (down from 460 million in FY2025, against a 200 million request, per the CRS figures for FY2025 and the request) and the fossil energy line at 720 million dollars, and did not fully reflect DOE's new structure. DOE's page for the new office, checked 2026-10-08, still lists a division for the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations and focus areas covering the Federal Energy Management Program and State and Community Energy Programs, so much of the work continues under new names. DOE announced termination of about 7.56 billion dollars in awards on 2025-10-01, and a court vacated some cancellations in June 2026.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14154 directs agencies to pause disbursement of funds appropriated under the IRA and IIJA pending review, which affects the programs run by these offices.

DOE announces it has terminated 321 financial awards supporting 223 projects, with estimated savings of about 7.56 billion dollars, issued by OCED, EERE, GDO, MESC, ARPA-E and Fossil Energy, after a case-by-case financial review (DOE release); S&P Global reports the action came on the first day of a government shutdown.

DOE publishes an organization chart dated 2025-11-20 that does not show EERE, FECM, GDO, OCED, SCEP, FEMP or MESC as stand-alone offices; it shows a new Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation, a Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Energy Office, an Office of Energy Dominance Financing and ARPA-E as a stand-alone office. Holland & Knight and Latitude Media describe where the programs moved, and DOE tied the changes to its energy dominance agenda.

Federation of American Scientists and American Nuclear Society analyses describe the chart; FAS says DOE's workforce fell by nearly a third over the prior year and about 350 projects received cancellation notices; ANS notes DOE did not say where the dropped offices' functions went.
Mintz reports DOE signaled the new structure may be revised after talks with authorizing committees in Congress (December 2025; exact day not confirmed, first of month used).

The FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations act, Division B of Public Law 119-74 (H.R. 6938, approved 2026-01-23 per govinfo), is enacted. The text of Division B was not readable, but Holland & Knight's summary of the passed bill reports no appropriation for OCED, EERE at 3.1 billion dollars (including reprogrammed funds), ARPA-E at 350 million and the fossil energy line at 720 million.
A federal judge in the District of Columbia vacates DOE's cancellation of 11 EERE grants worth 82.1 million dollars (date inferred from an article published 2026-06-12).

DOE's Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation page lists four divisions: critical minerals, energy technology, innovation/affordability/consumer choice (appliance standards, building codes, state and community programs), and the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations (page checked on this date; publication date not shown).

title: Eliminate DOE applied-energy and demonstration offices (EERE, OCED, GDO, FECM, ARPA-E)
uncertainties: DOE's 2025-11-20 organization chart was read through a fetch summary (the PDF is flattened, so reporting lines were not read). The text of Division B of Public Law 119-74 and its explanatory statement could not be read (the govinfo page stops partway through Division A), so FY2026 office funding levels still come from one law-firm table (Holland & Knight, written before signing); the CRS report R48599 (2025-12-30) covers only the request, House and Senate figures (EERE 3.46 billion in FY2025 and 888 million requested; ARPA-E 460 and 200 million; OCED 50 million in FY2025 and zero requested) and predates enactment. The two sources conflict on Grid Deployment Office funding (25 million versus 375 million dollars), so no GDO figure is used. ARPA-E's operating status is inferred from its stand-alone listing on the chart and its FY2026 appropriation; its website content could not be read. SCEP, FEMP and MESC funding outcomes were not retrieved. The 'dissolved' description of OCED in the appropriations summary conflicts with DOE's page listing an OCED division, and both are reported. The 7.56 billion dollar figure and the termination count (321 awards, 223 projects) come from DOE's 2025-10-01 release, and the 2026-06-11 ruling date is inferred from a Utility Dive article published 2026-06-12. No DOE press release announcing the reorganization was found; the chart is the DOE primary document.
